sections.html: Bangana behri is a bizarre carp from Southeast Asia, up to 45 cm long and related to Labeo. Adults develop a horn on the head and many tubercles on the face. Common name: Two-headed carp. Available size: 6-8 cm. Origin: Thailand.
In its native range, the Mekong basin, the species is a highly demanded food fish.
As it is a tropical species, water temperatures must not be under 20°C over a long period. The species might be an interesting candidate for heated koi ponds.
Bangana behri is reported to feed mainly on algae in the wild.

Like most Labeo-type fish, Bangana behri are somewhat quarrelsome towards conspecifics. In the importer's fishhouse about 30 specimens are kept together in one tank and live peacefully, but two or three specimens together can be expected not to do well. One should therefore keep them either solitary or in larger groups, a rule that holds for almost all fish related to Labeo.

Due to the unique head structure this species is also placed in the monotypical genus Incisilabeo; the full correct name is then Incisilabeo behri Fowler 1937.

Lexicon: Bangana: the native name for one of the species in Bengal. behri: dedication name for Otto Behr from Lopez, Sullivan County, Pennsylvania.

Along with Bangana behri came Labeo pierrei, which grows up to 80 cm and is listed as "vulnerable" on the IUCN Red List; catches of this much sought food fish are decreasing heavily.
